claims.text: Equimolar or nearly equimolar CoCrFeNiTi is the applicable composition.
The applicable equimolar CoCrFeNiTi starting material is a simple, single-phase solid solution.
The as-cast CoCrFeNiTi starting state is nanocrystalline.
The relatively low hardness and strength of the alloy arise from limited lattice distortion.
Limited lattice distortion produces weak solid-solution hardening.
Uniform elemental distribution creates a low-lattice-distortion environment in the simple solid solution.
The low lattice distortion is insufficient to impede dislocation motion significantly.
Grain-boundary-mediated deformation, including intergranular sliding, predominates over dislocation accumulation in the nanocrystalline state.
Predominant grain-boundary sliding limits strengthening from dislocation interactions and reduces resistance to plastic deformation.
Controlled annealing will increase grain size and reduce grain-boundary density.
Maintaining a highly nanocrystalline microstructure will yield lower hardness and strength because grain-boundary sliding remains predominant.
Annealing-induced grain growth will shift deformation toward dislocation-mediated plasticity.
Annealed, coarser-grained specimens will have greater hardness and yield strength than the as-cast nanocrystalline specimens.
The proposed mechanism applies at room temperature and moderate, controlled strain rates.
The nanocrystalline regime relevant to the hypothesis is typically below 50 nm grain size.
Comparing an as-cast nanocrystalline specimen with an annealed, coarser-grained specimen while keeping composition near equimolar provides the proposed control.
Failure of annealing to increase hardness and yield strength significantly would falsify the proposed mechanism.
Observation of predominantly dislocation-mediated plasticity in both grain-size conditions would falsify the proposed mechanism.
